sentence: This project develops a quantitative scan for imaging babies and uses it to identify babies with opioid exposure who have high risk for developmental delays.
This project studies how mixtures of air pollutants cause respiratory harm, using epidemiological studies together with cell-based toxicology.
This project supports prostate research projects with biostatistics and bioinformatics by helping them design studies, analyze data and store data.
This project uses biochemical assays and artificial intelligence to find the words in the instructions cells use to decide which genes are active.
This project tests whether dermal continuous sampling can show bioequivalence of topically applied drug products, instead of clinical endpoint studies.
This project studies what a group of transcription factors does in joints and how lowering them affects joint aging and osteoarthritis.
This project studies how aging and biological sex affect the latent reservoir of HIV in people on suppressive therapy, through hormones and inflammation.
This project uses human studies and zebrafish to find genes that link disorders of reproduction with disorders of craniofacial development.
This project studies the genes and clinical features of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder in children in Kenya and South Africa.
This project tries to find out how a long noncoding RNA found in T cells promotes T-cell proliferation in mice and humans.
This project tries to find out which initial factors govern stem cells and progenitors in forming new vessels after injury or disease.
This project uses deep learning to predict surgical skill scores from near infrared spectroscopy signals during surgical tasks.
This project uses imaging of mice and humans to study how menopause-related metabolic disruption causes neurodegeneration and whether hormone therapy helps.
This project studies cancers driven by viruses in people living with HIV in Tanzania, using cancer biology and genomics research.
This project uses Perturb-seq in mice to study how a signaling pathway in endothelial cells affects the risk of coronary artery disease.
This project studies how the niche in the larval gonad signals primordial germ cells to move from quiescence to proliferation.
This project studies how a recurrent genetic alteration drives peripheral T-cell lymphomas, using a genetically engineered mouse model and genomic profiling.
This project uses tissue-engineered human microvessels and imaging to study how angiogenesis is controlled in space and time.
This project builds small molecules that break down a tyrosine kinase fusion protein causing non-small cell lung cancer.
This project uses brain organoids grown from human induced pluripotent stem cells to study how voltage-gated sodium channels contribute to neurodevelopmental epilepsy.
